nuh: A very long time ago, there lived a people who forgot Allah. They made statues out of stones and began to worship them.
So Allah sent them His prophet Nuh, peace be upon him, calling them to worship Allah alone, by night and by day.
And Nuh kept calling them for nine hundred and fifty years, patient and never tired.
Then Allah commanded him to build a ship of planks and nails, under Allah's care and protection.
Whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him, while he kept working patiently.
Until Allah's command came, and the water began to gush.
Allah commanded him to carry in the ship a pair of every kind, and his family, except those who did not believe, and those who believed with him. And only a few believed with him.
Allah opened the gates of the sky with pouring water, and the earth burst with springs, and the waters met.
And the ship sailed with them through waves as high as mountains.

Nuh called to his son to ride with them, but he refused and said he would climb a mountain to save him from the water. Nuh said: Today nothing protects from Allah's command except His mercy. Then a wave came between them, and he was among the drowned.
Then the earth swallowed the water, the rain stopped, and the ship came to rest on Mount Judi.
Allah saved Nuh and those with him in the ship, and made it a sign for all people. We learned from Nuh: to be patient in doing good, and that obeying Allah is salvation.
yunus: Allah sent His prophet Yunus, peace be upon him, to his people, calling them to worship Allah alone.
They did not believe, so he warned them of punishment, but they did not turn back to their Lord.
He lost patience with them and left them angry, his heart heavy.
He boarded a ship full of passengers and goods.
Huge waves surrounded it, and the passengers feared they would drown.
They drew lots to lighten the ship, and the lot fell on Yunus.
He was thrown into the sea, and the whale swallowed him.
In the darkness of the night, the sea and the whale's belly, Yunus called on his Lord, repenting.
Allah answered his prayer, and the whale cast him onto empty land, his body weak.
Allah made a gourd plant grow over him to shade him.
And Allah sent him to a hundred thousand people or more, and they all believed.
We learned from Yunus: to be patient and not get angry, and that whoever calls on Allah sincerely in hardship, Allah saves him.
ibrahim: Allah gave Ibrahim, peace be upon him, guidance and wisdom.
His people worshipped idols they had made with their own hands.
He asked them about these idols, and they said: This is what our fathers used to do.
He told them that their Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them.
When his people went away, Ibrahim broke the idols into small pieces and left the biggest one.
The people came back, saw their idols smashed, and said: Who did this?
They brought Ibrahim before the people, and he said to them: Ask your idols, if they can speak.
They knew in themselves that the idols cannot speak, and can neither help nor harm.
But they grew angry, lit a huge fire, and threw Ibrahim into it.
The fire did not burn him, and no harm touched him in it.
They wanted evil for him, but Allah foiled their plot and made them the losers.
We learned from Ibrahim: to speak the truth bravely, and that Allah protects whoever trusts in Him.
musa: Allah commanded His prophet Musa, peace be upon him, to leave by night with those of the Children of Israel who believed with him.
When Pharaoh learned they had left, he sent his soldiers to gather his army from every city.
Pharaoh said: They are few, and we are ready for them.
Pharaoh and his soldiers went out after them and caught up with them at sunrise.
When each side saw the other, Musa's companions were afraid and said: Pharaoh will catch us.
Musa said: No, they will not reach us; Allah is with me and will guide me to the way of safety.
The sea split apart, each side like a great mountain, and dry paths appeared in it.
Musa and those with him crossed, not afraid of being caught or of drowning.
And Pharaoh and his soldiers entered the sea after them.
When Musa and those with him reached the shore, Allah closed the sea over Pharaoh and his soldiers, and they all drowned.
Allah saved Musa and all those with him, and it was a great sign.
We learned from Musa: whoever has Allah with him does not fear, and trusting Allah is salvation.
sulayman: Allah gave Dawud and Sulayman, peace be upon them, knowledge, and they praised Allah for His favour.
Sulayman inherited from his father Dawud prophethood, knowledge and kingship.
Allah taught him the speech of birds and gave him everything he needed.
Sulayman's armies of jinn, men and birds were gathered, marching in order.
Until they came to the Valley of the Ants.
An ant said: O ants, go into your homes, so that Sulayman and his soldiers do not crush you without knowing.
Sulayman smiled at her words, because she understood and warned her people.
He remembered Allah's blessing on him and called on his Lord in thanks.
We learned from Sulayman: to thank Allah for His blessings, and to be kind even to the smallest creatures.
salih: The people of Thamud lived among gardens, springs and palm trees, and carved houses out of the mountains.
Allah sent them their brother Salih, peace be upon him, calling them to worship Allah alone.
He said to them: Ask your Lord to forgive you, and turn back to Him; He is near and answers whoever calls Him.
They said: You are a man like us; bring us a sign if you are truthful.
So Allah gave him a she-camel, a sign of his truthfulness.
He said to them: The she-camel has a day to drink from the water, and you have a day to drink.
But they denied him, and the most wicked of them rose and killed the she-camel.
Salih said: Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days, then the punishment will come.
They woke up regretful, but their regret did not help them.
When Allah's command came, He saved Salih and those who believed with him by His mercy.
The Blast seized the wrongdoers, and their homes became empty as if they had never lived there.
We learned from Salih: to respect Allah's signs, and to be kind to animals and never hurt them.
hud: The people of Aad lived in al-Ahqaf, great sands in the south of Arabia.
Allah sent them their brother Hud, peace be upon him, calling them to worship Allah alone.
He said to them: I ask no reward from you; my reward is with Allah who created me.
Ask your Lord's forgiveness and turn to Him; He will send rain upon you and add to your strength.
They said: We will not leave our gods because of your words, and we do not believe you.
Hud said: I rely on Allah; He is my Lord and your Lord.
When they saw a huge cloud heading to their valleys, they rejoiced and said: This cloud brings us rain.
A bitterly cold wind blew for seven nights and eight days in a row.
It destroyed everything Allah commanded it to, and nothing remained after it but their empty houses.
Allah saved Hud and those who believed with him by His mercy.
We learned from Hud: to rely on Allah, and that asking forgiveness brings goodness.
ayyub: Ayyub, peace be upon him, was a righteous servant; Allah gave him family, children and wealth.
Then Allah tested him with a severe illness in his body, and he lost his family, his wealth and his children.
Ayyub was patient, content with what Allah decreed, and complained only to his Lord.
The days passed and he stayed patient, remembering Allah and turning to Him.
Then he called on his Lord: O my Lord, tiredness and pain have touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
Allah answered his prayer and said to him: Strike the ground with your foot.
Cool water sprang from the ground; he drank from it and washed, and the illness left him.
Allah gave him back his family, and as many again with them, as a mercy from Him.
Allah praised him and said: We found him patient, what an excellent servant.
Allah made him an example for everyone who is patient and hopes for his Lord's mercy.
We learned from Ayyub: to be patient when we are ill or sad, and to call on Allah, for after patience comes relief.
zakariya: Zakariya, peace be upon him, was a righteous prophet who cared for Maryam and gave her a place in his prayer room.
Every time he went in to her, he found good food with her, and asked: Where did you get this? She said: It is from Allah.
Zakariya had grown old, his bones weak and his hair white, and his wife could not have children.
When he saw how Allah honoured Maryam, he quietly asked his Lord to give him a righteous child.
While he stood praying in his prayer room, the good news came: he would have a son named Yahya.
Allah had not given anyone that name before him.
Zakariya wondered with joy: How can I have a son when I am old and my wife cannot have children?
He was told: That is easy for Allah; He created you before when you were nothing.
His sign was that he could not speak to people for three days, though he was healthy and well.
He went out to his people and signed to them: Glorify Allah morning and evening.
Yahya was born, and while still young Allah commanded him to hold the Torah firmly: to learn it, understand it and act on it.
Allah gave him wisdom while still young; he was gentle and obedient to his Lord.
He was good to his parents and obeyed them, and he was neither arrogant nor disobedient.
We learned from Zakariya and Yahya: to call on Allah and never lose hope, and to be good to our fathers and mothers.
kaaba: Allah commanded Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he settled his son Ismail and his mother Hajar in the valley of Makkah.
It was a valley with no crops and no water, next to Allah's House.
When Ibrahim turned to leave, Hajar asked him: Did Allah command you to do this? He said: Yes. She said: Then He will not let us be lost.
Ibrahim prayed to his Lord to make people's hearts long for them and to provide them with fruits, so that they would give thanks.
He prayed that Makkah be a safe land, and that Allah keep him and his sons away from worshipping idols. And Allah answered his prayer.
When the water ran out, Hajar grew thirsty, and so did her son.
She climbed Mount Safa to see if she could see anyone, then went to Marwa, and did that seven times. The Prophet ﷺ said: That is why people walk between them.
Then she found the angel at the place of Zamzam; he dug the ground until water appeared.
She drank and nursed her child, and the angel said to her: Do not fear being lost; here is the House of Allah, which this boy and his father will build.
Then Allah showed Ibrahim the place of the House and commanded him to build it.
Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the Kaaba, stone upon stone, calling on Allah humbly.
Ibrahim stood on a stone while building; it is the Station of Ibrahim, where we pray.
They prayed to Allah to keep them firm in Islam, and to make from their children a Muslim nation.
They prayed that Allah send among their children a messenger to teach them the Quran; that was our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, from the children of Ismail.
Allah commanded them to purify His House for those who go around it and those who pray.
Then Allah commanded him to call people to Hajj, and they come on foot and riding, from every distant road.
Allah made the Kaaba a place people return to, and a place of safety for them.
We learned from Ibrahim and Ismail: to obey Allah and trust Him, and to do our work well and ask Allah to accept it.
ilyas: Allah honoured His servant Ilyas, peace be upon him, with prophethood and sent him to his people of the Children of Israel.
They worshipped an idol and abandoned the worship of Allah.
He said to them: Fear Allah alone, and do not worship anyone besides Him.
How can you worship an idol and leave the worship of Allah, the Best of creators?
Allah is your Lord, who created you and created your forefathers before you.
His people denied him, except Allah's servants who were sincere in their religion; they are saved.
Allah gave Ilyas a good mention among the nations after him; peace from Allah be upon him.
That is how Allah rewards those who do good; he was one of His sincere believing servants.
We learned from Ilyas: to worship Allah who created us, and to say the truth even if people disagree with us.
kahf: There were some young men who believed in their Lord, and Allah increased them in guidance and firmness on the truth.
Their people worshipped idols and wanted to force them to worship them too.
Allah strengthened their hearts, and they stood up and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; we will never worship anyone else.
Then they left their people and took shelter in a cave in the mountain, to worship their Lord alone.
They prayed to their Lord to have mercy on them and to make the right way easy for them.
Allah sent a deep sleep over them in the cave.
When the sun rose, it turned away from their cave, and when it set, it passed them by, so its heat did not harm them.
Allah turned them while they slept, once on the right side and once on the left.
Their dog, who kept them company, lay with its forelegs stretched out at the cave's entrance.
They slept for three hundred and nine years.
Then Allah woke them as they were, and they asked one another: How long did we sleep? They said: A day or part of a day.
Others said: Your Lord knows best how long you slept.
They sent one of them with their silver coins to the city, to buy good, lawful food, and to be careful so that no one would recognise them.
When the seller saw their old coins, their secret came out, and people learned their story.
People knew that Allah's promise is true, and that Allah raises people after death, just as He woke the young men after a long sleep.
We learned from the people of the cave: to stay firm on the truth even if people around us are not, and that whoever takes refuge in Allah, He protects him.
luqman: Luqman was a righteous servant; Allah gave him wisdom: understanding of the religion, a sound mind and the right word.
Allah commanded him to thank Him for His blessings, and whoever gives thanks only benefits himself.
Luqman sat advising his son and said: My dear son, do not worship anything besides Allah; that is the greatest sin.
Allah commanded us to be good to our parents and kind to them; our mothers carried us in weakness upon weakness, and nursed us for two years.
So we thank Allah, and then we thank our parents.
Luqman said: My dear son, even if a deed is as small as a mustard seed, inside a rock, in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it out.
Allah is gentle with His servants and knows all their deeds.
My dear son, establish the prayer, call to good, forbid evil with gentleness and kindness, and be patient with whatever befalls you.
Do not turn your face away from people when they speak to you, and do not walk on the earth proudly; Allah does not love the arrogant.
Be humble in your walk, and lower your voice; do not raise it.
We learned from Luqman: to worship Allah alone, to be good to our fathers and mothers, to pray, to be humble, and to speak politely.
fil: Abraha of Abyssinia came with an army and an elephant, wanting to destroy the blessed Kaaba.
But Allah ruined the evil they had planned.
Allah sent against them birds in flock after flock.
Pelting them with stones of hardened clay.
And they became like dry, eaten-up leaves.
We learned from the people of the elephant: that Allah is All-Powerful, and that He ruins the plots of the wrongdoers however strong they are.
yusuf: When Yusuf, peace be upon him, was young, he saw in a dream eleven stars and the sun and the moon bowing to him.
His father Yaqub said to him: My dear son, do not tell your dream to your brothers, or they will envy you.
His brothers used to say: Our father loves Yusuf and his brother more than us, and they agreed to take him away from his father.
They took him with them to the pastures and threw him into a well.
Allah revealed to Yusuf: One day you will tell them what they did.
They came back to their father at night crying and said: The wolf ate him, and they brought his shirt with false blood on it.
Yaqub said: No, you have planned something bad; I will be patient, complaining only to Allah, and I seek His help.
A caravan passed by and sent someone to fetch water; when he let down his bucket, Yusuf held on to it.
They sold him for a few coins and took him to Egypt, where the Aziz bought him and said to his wife: Treat him well.
When Yusuf grew up, Allah gave him understanding and knowledge, because he was one of those who do good.
Then Yusuf was put in prison unjustly, though innocent; in prison he called his two companions to worship Allah alone and explained their dreams.
The king of Egypt saw in a dream seven fat cows eaten by seven thin ones, and seven green ears of grain and others dry.
Yusuf explained it: seven years of plenty, so store the grain in its ears, then seven hard years in which you eat what you stored.
Then a year will come in which rain falls and there is plenty.
When his innocence became clear, the king took him out of prison and brought him close; Yusuf said: Put me in charge of the storehouses of Egypt, for I am trustworthy and knowing.
The hard years came, and his brothers came to Egypt asking for food; he recognised them, but they did not recognise him.
He treated them generously and asked them to bring their brother from their father; when they brought him, he drew him close and told him secretly: I am your brother, so do not be sad.
Then he revealed to his brothers that he was Yusuf, that this was his brother, and that Allah had honoured them and brought them together; whoever fears Allah and is patient, Allah rewards his good.
They said: Allah has favoured you above us, and we were wrong.
He sent his shirt to his father, and when it was laid on his face, his sight came back.

Yaqub and his family came to Egypt; Yusuf seated his parents on his throne to honour them, and his parents and brothers bowed to him as a greeting, not as worship; that was allowed in their law, and it is forbidden in ours.
Yusuf said: My father, this is the meaning of the dream I saw when I was young, and my Lord has made it come true.
We learned from Yusuf: to be patient and fear Allah, and to forgive those who wronged us, for Allah rewards those who do good.
shuayb: Allah sent to the people of Madyan their brother Shuayb, peace be upon him.
He said to them: My people, worship Allah alone; you have no god other than Him.
They used to give short measure and weight, taking from people's rights when they sold.
He said to them: Give full measure and weight with justice, do not cheat people of what is theirs, and do not spread corruption on earth.
He said: What remains for you of lawful profit is better for you than unlawful gain.
They mocked him and said: Does your prayer tell you that we must leave what our fathers worshipped, and not do with our money as we like?
Shuayb said: I only want to set you right as much as I can, and only Allah helps me in that; on Him I rely.
He never told them to do something and then did otherwise himself.
But they insisted and said: We do not understand much of what you say.
When Allah's command came, He saved Shuayb and those who believed with him by His mercy, and the Blast seized the wrongdoers.
We learned from Shuayb: to be honest in buying and selling, not to cheat or take anyone's right, and that the lawful is better than the unlawful.
musa_baby: Musa, peace be upon him, was born, and his mother feared for him from Pharaoh.
Allah inspired her: Nurse him calmly, and if you fear for him, put him in a box and place it in the Nile.
Do not fear and do not grieve; Allah will return him to you and make him a messenger.
She put him in a box and placed it in the Nile, and said to his sister: Follow him.
His sister followed him, watching him from afar, and they did not know she was his sister.
Pharaoh's helpers found him and took him.
When Pharaoh's wife saw him, Allah put love for him in her heart, and she said: Do not kill him; perhaps we can take him as a son.
Musa's mother's heart was full of worry for him, but Allah made her steady and she was patient.
Musa would not nurse from any woman they brought to him.
His sister said: I know a family who will look after him, nurse him and be good to him. And they agreed.
So Allah returned him to his mother, so that she would be happy and not grieve, and know that Allah keeps His promise.
We learned from Musa's mother: to trust Allah's promise, for Allah never breaks His promise.
dayf: Strange guests came to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and said: Peace, and he replied: Peace.
He did not know they were noble angels.
He went quickly to his family and brought them a fat roasted calf, and offered it kindly: Will you not eat?
When he saw that they did not eat, he felt afraid of them.
They said: Do not be afraid; we are angels of Allah, sent to the people of Lut.
His wife Sarah was standing behind the curtain listening, and they gave her the good news of a son named Ishaq, and after him a grandson named Yaqub.
She was amazed: How can I have a son when I am an old woman and my husband is an old man?
They said to her: Do not be amazed at Allah's command; He is able to do all things.
They said: Thus has your Lord said; He is able to do it, the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.
They gave Ibrahim the good news that this son would be a man of knowledge of Allah.
We learned from Ibrahim: to honour guests, to return a greeting with a better one, and that nothing is beyond Allah's power.
sabt: There was a town near the sea; Allah commanded its people to honour the Sabbath and not to fish on it.
Allah tested them: on the Sabbath the fish came to them in great numbers, floating on the surface of the sea.
When the Sabbath was over, the fish went away, and they saw none of them.
Some of them played a trick: they trapped the fish in pits on the Sabbath and caught them afterwards.
A righteous group stood up to advise them and forbid them from disobeying Allah.
A third group said to them: Why do you advise people whom Allah will destroy?
They said: We advise them to do what Allah commanded us, and so that they may fear Allah and repent.
When the wrongdoers did not listen to the advice, Allah saved those who had forbidden the disobedience.
And He punished the wrongdoers, turning them into apes, kept far from all good.
We learned from the people of the Sabbath: not to play tricks with Allah's command, and to advise gently, for advice saves the one who gives it.
ihya: A man passed by a town whose houses had fallen down, and said: How will Allah bring this town back to life after its death?
So Allah made him die for a hundred years, then brought him back to life and asked him: How long did you stay? He said: A day or part of a day.
He told him he had stayed a hundred years, and told him to look at his food and drink: they had not changed in all that time.
And to look at his donkey, how Allah brings it back to life after it had become bones.
When he saw that with his own eyes, he was certain that Allah is able to do all things.
Ibrahim, peace be upon him, asked his Lord to show him how He gives life to the dead, to add certainty to his certainty.
Allah commanded him to take four birds and put a part of them on each mountain, then call them.
Ibrahim called, and every part went back to its place, and the birds came rushing.
Allah is Almighty, nothing overcomes Him, and Wise in all He does.
We learned from the two signs: that Allah who created us the first time is able to give us life after death, and to ask so that we grow in certainty.
hudhud: Sulayman, peace be upon him, checked on the birds and did not find the hoopoe, and said: Why do I not see the hoopoe?
He wanted to know its excuse for being away.
The hoopoe came soon after and said: I have come to you from Saba in Yemen with certain news.
I found a woman ruling them, and she has a great throne.
I found her and her people bowing to the sun, not worshipping Allah.
Sulayman said: We will see whether you told the truth or not; take this letter of mine to them.
The hoopoe dropped the letter to the queen; she gathered the leaders of her people and said: A noble letter has reached me.
In it was: Do not be arrogant, and come to me submitting to Allah.
She consulted her people, then sent Sulayman a gift of precious wealth.
Sulayman said: What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you, and he did not accept the gift.
Then he said: Which of you will bring me her throne? A man whom Allah had given knowledge said: I will bring it to you before you blink. He called on Allah, and the throne came.
When Sulayman saw it before him, he said: This is from Allah's favour to me, to test me: will I thank Him for His blessing or deny it?
When the queen came, she saw Allah's power and Sulayman's truthfulness, and said: I submit with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
We learned from the hoopoe: to tell the truth and to call to Allah. And from Sulayman: to thank Allah for every blessing.
adam: Allah said to the angels: I am placing on the earth people who will succeed one another to build it.
The angels asked about the wisdom in that, and Allah told them that He knows what they do not know.
Allah taught Adam the names of all things, then showed them to the angels, and they said: We know only what You have taught us, our Lord.
And Adam told them their names.
Allah commanded the angels to bow to Adam as a greeting and an honour, and they all bowed, except Iblis, who refused out of pride and envy.
Allah let Adam and his wife Hawwa live in Paradise and allowed them to eat whatever fruit they wished, except one tree that He forbade them.
In it you will not be hungry or bare, nor thirsty, nor touched by the heat of the sun.
Allah warned him: Iblis is an enemy to you both, so beware that he does not cause you to leave Paradise.
But Satan whispered to them and claimed that this tree would make them live forever, and swore he was their sincere adviser, while he was lying.
They ate from the tree, and Adam forgot the advice.
They regretted it, and called on their Lord admitting their sin, asking Him to forgive them and have mercy on them.
Allah accepted Adam's repentance and forgave him; He is the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.
Then Allah chose him, brought him close and guided him.
Allah sent them down to the earth and promised them that guidance would come to them; whoever follows it will not fear or grieve.
We learned from Adam: that Satan is our enemy, and that when we make a mistake we return to Allah and ask His forgiveness, for He is the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.
isa: Maryam was a righteous woman, whom Allah chose above the women of the worlds.
She went away from her family to a place towards the east, and put a screen between herself and them.
Allah sent the angel Jibril to her, and she sought refuge in the Most Merciful from him.
He said to her: I am only a messenger from your Lord, come to give you the good news of a pure boy.
She wondered: How can I have a child when I have no husband? He said: That is easy for Allah; when He wills something, He says to it: Be, and it is.
Allah created him without a father, to be a sign for people of Allah's power, and a mercy from Him.
The time of birth came by the trunk of a palm tree, and she was called: Do not grieve; Allah has made a stream flow beneath you.
Shake the trunk of the palm tree, and fresh ripe dates will fall on you; so eat, drink and be at peace.
Then she came to her people carrying him, and they blamed her, so she pointed to him.
They said: How can we talk to a baby in the cradle? And Isa spoke while still a baby.
He said: Allah has made me blessed wherever I am, commanded me to pray and give zakat, and made me good to my mother.
When he grew up, Allah sent him to the Children of Israel and taught him the Torah and the Injil.
Allah gave him miracles: he shaped clay like a bird, breathed into it, and it became a bird by Allah's permission.
He healed those born blind and those with leprosy, and brought the dead to life by Allah's permission.
All of this shows that he is Allah's prophet and messenger, and that he is Allah's servant.
We learned from Isa and his mother: that Allah is able to do all things, and to be good to our mothers and keep up the prayer.
dhulqarnayn: Dhul-Qarnayn was a righteous king; Allah gave him power on earth and gave him the means and ways to everything.
He used those means with effort and hard work.
He travelled until he reached the setting of the sun, and saw it as if it were setting in a hot spring of black mud, and he found a people there.
He ruled among them with justice: whoever believed and did good, he was good to him and spoke gently to him.
Then he travelled to the east, and found the sun rising on a people who had no building to cover them and no trees to shade them.
Then he travelled until he came between two mountains, and found a people who could hardly understand the speech of others.
They said: Yajuj and Majuj spread corruption on earth; shall we collect money for you so that you build a barrier between us and them?
He said: What my Lord has given me is better than your money, but help me with your strength.
They brought pieces of iron and put them between the two mountains until they were level with them.
They lit a fire until all the iron was glowing, then he poured copper over it.
It became a high, smooth barrier; they could not climb over it or dig through it.
Dhul-Qarnayn was not proud; instead he said: This barrier is a mercy from Allah to the people.
We learned from Dhul-Qarnayn: to use the means and work hard, to be just, and to give credit to Allah, not to ourselves.
jannatayn: This is a parable Allah told us about two men: one a believer and the other a disbeliever.
The disbeliever had two vineyards, surrounded by many palm trees, with crops between them.
Each garden gave its full fruit, and a river ran between them, watering them.
The owner of the two gardens was filled with pride and said to his believing companion: I have more wealth than you and stronger supporters.
He went into his garden, admired its fruit and said: I do not think this garden will ever be destroyed.
And he said: I do not think the Hour will come.
His believing companion advised him: How can you disbelieve in Allah who created you from dust, then made you a complete human being?
As for me, I say: Allah alone is my Lord, and I associate no one with Him.
Why did you not remember Allah and thank Him when you entered your garden and admired it? It is from His favour, not from your power.
What his companion had warned him of came true, and everything in the garden was destroyed.
He began wringing his hands in regret over what he had spent on it, wishing he had worshipped Allah alone and associated no one with Him.
And he found no one to help him among those he used to boast about.
We learned from the owner of the two gardens: to thank Allah for His blessings and not be deceived, and to remember Allah when something pleases us, as we heard in the verse.
dawud: After the time of Musa, the Children of Israel asked their prophet to appoint a king for them, to fight with him against the enemies who had driven them from their homes.
Their prophet told them that Allah had chosen Talut as their king.
They said: How can he be king when he does not have much wealth? He said: Allah chose him and gave him more knowledge and strength.
Talut set out with his soldiers and said to them: Allah will test you with a river; whoever drinks from it is not one of my companions, except whoever takes only a handful.
When they reached the river, most of them drank, except a few who were patient with their thirst.
Talut crossed with the few believers, and they saw Jalut and his many soldiers.
The believers said: Many a small, patient group has defeated a large one with Allah's help and support, and Allah helps the patient.
They called on their Lord to pour patience into their hearts, make their feet firm, and give them victory.
Allah gave them victory over their enemy, and Dawud, peace be upon him, killed Jalut.
After that Allah gave Dawud kingship and prophethood, and taught him what He willed.
The mountains and the birds would glorify Allah with him when he glorified Him.
Allah made iron soft for him, like dough, and he made from it armour that protects whoever wears it.
We learned from Dawud and Talut's companions: that victory comes from Allah, and that Allah helps the patient.
dhabih: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, prayed to his Lord: My Lord, give me a righteous child.
Allah answered him and gave him the good news of a forbearing boy: Ismail.
When Ismail grew old enough to walk with his father, his father said to him: I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so what do you think?
The dreams of prophets are true, a command from Allah.
Ismail, dutiful to his father, said: My father, do what Allah has commanded you, and you will find me patient, if Allah wills.
When they both submitted to Allah's command, Allah called to him: O Ibrahim, you have fulfilled the dream and done what you were commanded.
This was a great test, in which the truth of his faith became clear.
Allah saved Ismail and put a great ram in his place.
That is how Allah rewards those who do good, saving them from hardships.
Allah left for Ibrahim a good mention among the nations after him; peace be upon Ibrahim.
Then Allah gave him the good news of his son Ishaq, a prophet among the righteous, as a reward for his patience, and blessed them both.
That ram was a sacrifice and a practice until the Day of Resurrection; that is why we sacrifice at Eid al-Adha.
We learned from Ibrahim and Ismail: to obey Allah and be good to our parents, and that whoever is patient with Allah's command, Allah gives him a way out.
khidr: Musa, peace be upon him, set out with his young helper Yusha ibn Nun, wanting to meet a righteous servant and learn from him knowledge he did not have.
They had a dead fish with them as food; when they sat by a rock where the two seas meet, the fish came alive and slipped into the sea.

When they had gone far and grew hungry, the helper remembered the fish, and Musa said: That is what we were looking for; it is the sign of the righteous servant's place. So they went back to the rock.
There they found al-Khidr, peace be upon him, to whom Allah had given mercy from Himself and taught great knowledge.
Musa greeted him and said: Will you allow me to follow you so that you teach me?
Al-Khidr said: You will not be patient with what you see from me; how can you be patient with things whose wisdom you do not know?
Musa said: I will be patient, if Allah wills, and I will not disobey you in anything.
Al-Khidr said: Then do not ask me about anything until I explain it to you. So they set off and boarded a ship whose owners carried them for free, and al-Khidr damaged it by pulling out a plank.
Musa said: Did you damage it to drown its people? Al-Khidr reminded him of his condition, and Musa apologised and asked him to forgive him because he had forgotten.
Then Musa saw something else, even harder, and objected to it, then said: If I ask you again after this, do not keep me with you.
They came to a town and asked for food, but no one welcomed them as guests; they found a leaning wall about to fall, and al-Khidr set it straight.
Musa said: If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it to buy food. Al-Khidr said: Here we part, and I will tell you the wisdom of what you could not be patient with.
As for the ship, it belonged to poor people who worked at sea, and ahead of them was a king who seized every sound ship by force, so I damaged it so that it would be safe for them.

As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys, and beneath it was money buried for them; their father had been a righteous man, so Allah wanted them to grow up and take out their money, as a mercy from Him to them.
And I did none of this on my own; I did it by Allah's command.
We learned from Musa and al-Khidr: to seek knowledge humbly, that behind what we do not understand there is wisdom Allah knows, and that the goodness of parents benefits their children.
